notes: Expected shared-prior misreads, in order of damage moved: (1) ACID INSTANCING — the engine appends an independent DoT per fire and never dedups; jill's reload cycle is ~2.1s (9-round mag, 81f reload) against a 30s duration, so naive per-reload encoding stacks ~14 concurrent 192%/s instances (~2700%/s, dwarfing her 71.09% normals). Design arithmetic strongly implies maintained/refresh (one live instance); whether the real game stacks is a measurement question — the test must pin ≤1 tick/sec regardless of encoding, and the stacking claim must not be resolved by assumption in either direction. (2) The kit deliberately SPLITS trigger identities: skill1's 34.99 is burstCast ('when using Burst Skill') while skill2's 40.03 is fullBurstEnter ('when entering Full Burst') — a driver applying one prior to both lines fails one direction or the other, and controlComp's helm co-B3 is exactly the fixture that separates them (assert per-rotation apply counts both ways). (3) Reload lines ARE damage: the 99.96 reload buff + 100% ammo dump + forced reload is the burst's re-arm combo (fresh Magnum + fresh Acid inside the FB window); dropping any of the three as QoL/flavor breaks the loop (Grave reload-drop precedent). Note 'fixed at' is formally a clamp primitive, benign in controlComp but worth a caveat. (4) True-normals conversion has no bare schema primitive outside weaponSwap.trueNormals — whatever encoding ships, assert the EVENT contract (window normals true-flavored, fed by the 34.99) not the encoding. (5) ALWAYS-⚑: AR cadence tuple (datamine-unreliable) and the Hit-Rate→core slope (measured-only) must ship flagged; the 80.78 stat value itself is kit-stated. (6) Inertness: every line is self-or-boss scoped — a cheap high-value assertion is that zeroing jill's override moves no ally's total.
